settingsAddLimitTitle.description: Heading over the form that creates a new site limit.

settingsAdvancedFeaturesNote.message: Switching one of these makes the level above read "Custom". Nothing is lost: picking a level again replaces the selection.
settingsAdvancedFeaturesNote.description: Note under the "Individual changes" heading, saying what happens to the preset control when a single switch is moved.

settingsAdvancedFeaturesTitle.description: Heading inside Advanced, over the eight per-feature switches that the three presets above set in one go.

settingsAdvancedPacksTitle.description: Heading inside Advanced, over the per-image-service switches.

settingsAdvancedSummary.description: Label on the collapsed disclosure holding the individual optimizer switches, the per-image-service switches and the savings measurement rate.

settingsAdvancedSummaryNote.description: Note beside the "Advanced" disclosure label, saying what is inside it. Lower case, as a continuation of the label.

settingsAlertPlanHint.message: On by default: a plan running out is the thing nobody is watching for.
settingsAlertPlanHint.description: Hint under the plan alerts switch, giving the reason it ships on. It no longer says "from the plan above": the plan is now its own section rather than the panel above this one.

settingsAlertPlanLabel.description: Switch turning on notifications for the allowance that covers every site.

settingsAlertSitesHint.message: Off by default: a limit you typed on a site you chose is one you expect to reach.
settingsAlertSitesHint.description: Hint under the per-site alerts switch, giving the reason it ships off.

settingsAlertSitesLabel.description: Switch turning on notifications for per-site limits.

settingsAlertsNoAllowance.message: Plan alerts are on, but there is no allowance over everything for them to measure: set a plan size under Data plan and choose "$SHED$" or "$STOP$".
settingsAlertsNoAllowance.description: Appended to the threshold sentence when plan alerts are on with nothing to alert on — the default state of a fresh install. SHED and STOP name the two options that create an allowance.

settingsAlertsReadError.message: Could not read the alert settings.
settingsAlertsReadError.description: Fallback error when the alert settings cannot be loaded.

settingsAlertsSaveError.message: Could not save the alert settings.
settingsAlertsSaveError.description: Fallback error when an alert setting cannot be written.

settingsAlertsSub.message: A desktop notification when an allowance is running out, said once and not repeated.
settingsAlertsSub.description: One line under the "Alerts" heading, bounding how often a notification can arrive.

settingsAlertsThresholds.message: Thresholds are fixed at $THRESHOLDS$, and only the highest one crossed is sent — one large download cannot produce three notifications at once.
settingsAlertsThresholds.description: States when a notification is sent. The thresholds are printed from the alerting module rather than typed, so the sentence cannot come to describe a ladder that is no longer used.

settingsAlertsTitle.description: Heading of the section choosing which allowances raise a desktop notification.

settingsAllowanceChangeError.description: Fallback error when writing the allowance that covers every site fails.

settingsAllowanceLabel.description: Heading of the card showing the budget that covers every site, as opposed to a single-site limit.

settingsAllowanceResets.description: Note beside the allowance-over-everything heading: the window the allowance covers, and when it restarts.

settingsAllowanceTier.description: What the allowance is currently refusing: the short name of the step, then the sentence explaining what it costs.

detail.example: Video and audio segments are refused. Players usually drop to a lower quality or pause.

settingsAppearanceAdvancedNote.message: units, and how weeks and months are counted
settingsAppearanceAdvancedNote.description: Note beside the "Advanced" disclosure label in the Appearance section, saying what is inside it. Lower case, as a continuation of the label.

settingsAppearanceSub.message: How Byte Budget looks, and what it shows on the Chrome toolbar.

settingsAppearanceTitle.description: Heading of the section holding theme and the toolbar badge. Units and the week/month rules moved inside its Advanced disclosure, so they are no longer named in the heading.

settingsBadgeLabel.description: Label for the picker choosing what figure is drawn on the extension's toolbar icon.

settingsBadgeOff.description: Toolbar badge option: draw nothing on the icon.

settingsBadgeSession.description: Toolbar badge option: show the total for this browsing session.

settingsBadgeToday.description: Toolbar badge option: show today's total.

settingsBrandTitle.description: Page heading, under the product name in the page header.

settingsCancel.description: Button that abandons an edit or a pending deletion without changing anything.

settingsCycleTitle.description: Heading over the block showing how far into the current plan cycle you are and how much of the allowance is spent.

settingsDataSub.message: Every usage figure stays in this browser profile. If you connect a Plus account, Byte Budget also checks its status with ExtensionPay.
settingsDataSub.description: PRIVACY DISCLOSURE, shortened to one line under the heading. The full statement is behind the "What is recorded" disclosure and is the one that must match the published policy; this line may not claim anything that one does not.

settingsDataTitle.description: Heading of the section describing what is stored, and holding export and delete.

settingsDeleteButton.description: Button that arms the deletion. It does not delete on its own — a second button confirms.

settingsDeleteConfirm.description: Second button, which performs the deletion. Worded so it cannot be pressed by reflex.

settingsDeleteError.description: Fallback error when the deletion fails.

settingsDeleteScope.message: This deletes every recorded byte count in this profile: the daily and hourly rows, the per-host rows, one row per page load, the learned size estimator and the observed image sizes. Limits, exceptions and the settings on this page are kept. To remove only the older days instead, shorten "$SETTING$" above.
settingsDeleteScope.description: Says what deletion removes and what it leaves, and offers the narrower alternative. SETTING is the name of the retention control, so the sentence points at a control the reader can see.

settingsDeleteScopeKept.message: This deletes every recorded byte count in this profile: the daily and hourly rows, the per-host rows, one row per page load, the learned size estimator and the observed image sizes. Limits, exceptions and the settings on this page are kept. To remove only the older days instead, shorten "$SETTING$" above — it is $KEPT$ now.
settingsDeleteScopeKept.description: The same sentence as settingsDeleteScope, with the current retention value appended. Kept as one whole message rather than a sentence plus a tail, so the clause can be placed wherever the language needs it.

settingsDeleteWarning.message: This cannot be undone, and nothing is exported first.
settingsDeleteWarning.description: Shown once deletion is armed. Two steps in the page rather than a modal dialog, because a dialog is read as boilerplate.

settingsDeleted.message: Deleted. Every limit now starts its current window from zero.
settingsDeleted.description: Confirmation after deletion. The second sentence is a consequence, not reassurance: the counters limits are checked against have restarted.

settingsDeleting.description: Shown while the deletion is running.

settingsEditAmountAria.description: Accessible name for the number field in the inline allowance editor.

settingsEditSave.description: Submit button in the inline allowance editor.

settingsEditSaved.description: Confirmation after changing an existing allowance in place.

settingsEditSizeInvalid.message: Give the allowance a size above zero.
settingsEditSizeInvalid.description: Error when the inline allowance editor is submitted with a blank, zero or negative number.

settingsEditUnitAria.description: Accessible name for the byte-unit dropdown beside the number field in the inline allowance editor.

settingsExceptionsAdd.description: Submit button for the form adding a site to the exception list.

settingsExceptionsInputLabel.description: Accessible name for the field that adds a site to the exception list. Not shown on screen.

settingsExceptionsIntro.message: Leave a site completely alone: no rules, no page script, no rewritten images. This is the first thing to try if a site looks wrong.
settingsExceptionsIntro.description: Explains what excluding a site does, and offers it as the first remedy for a broken page.

settingsExceptionsLabel.description: Heading for the list of sites Data Saver leaves completely alone.

settingsExceptionsPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the field for adding a site to leave alone. A domain name.

settingsExclusionDuplicate.description: Shown when the site typed into the exception form is already on the list.

settingsExclusionRemoveAria.description: Accessible name for the button that removes one site from the exception list. Names what pressing it does, not what the site currently is.

settingsExclusionsCount.description: Count beside the "Website exceptions" heading when at least one site is excepted.

settingsExclusionsNone.description: Count beside the "Website exceptions" heading when no site is excepted.

settingsExportCsv.description: Button downloading the usage table as a CSV file.

settingsExportError.description: Fallback error when an export fails.

settingsExportHint.message: One row per site per day, as stored: the date, the site, bytes down and up, requests, and how much of the down figure was estimated rather than measured.
settingsExportHint.description: Describes the shape of an exported file, column by column.

settingsExportJson.description: Button downloading the usage table as a JSON file.

settingsExportRangeDays.description: One option in the export range dropdown.

settingsExportRangeDaysLocked.description: An export range the free tier cannot choose. A <select> option cannot carry a padlock or a tooltip, so the label says it instead. Pairs with settingsExportRangeDays, which is the same option when it is available.

settingsExportRangeLabel.description: Accessible name for the dropdown choosing how many days an export covers. Not shown on screen.

settingsExportWrote.description: Confirmation after an export, naming the file that was downloaded.

settingsFeatureSaveDataNote.message: Cost: it also makes this browser easier to recognise. Desktop Chrome has no setting that sends this header, so sending it is a rare, stable signal a tracker can use. It is on by default; the image services below remove the same kind of bytes without announcing anything.
settingsFeatureSaveDataNote.description: Privacy disclosure attached to the Save-Data optimizer, stating what sending the header costs. The privacy policy describes this control, so the wording has to keep saying that the header is a fingerprinting signal. Do not soften it.

settingsFlushError.message: The last write that failed was $WHEN$: $REASON$. Those counts were put back in the buffer and retried, so they are not lost — but every total read between then and the retry was low by that much.
settingsFlushError.description: Admission that a write to the ledger failed. REASON is the browser's own error text and is not translated. Keep the last clause: it says the figures on screen were wrong for a while, which is the part a reader needs.

settingsFlushErrorChip.description: Chip introducing the report of a failed write to the ledger.

settingsGrantDay.description: Button adding bytes to a limit's current window, where the window is one day.

settingsGrantMonth.description: Button adding bytes to a limit's current window, where the window is one month.

settingsGrantSession.description: Button adding bytes to a limit's current window, where the window is this browsing session.

settingsGrantTitleSession.message: Raises the allowance to $TOTAL$ until it resets. Only for this session.
settingsGrantTitleSession.description: Tooltip on the add-bytes button for a session limit, stating the resulting allowance before the click.

settingsGrantTitleWindow.message: Raises the allowance to $TOTAL$ until it resets. Only for this window.
settingsGrantTitleWindow.description: Tooltip on the add-bytes button for a day, week or month limit, stating the resulting allowance before the click.

settingsGrantWeek.description: Button adding bytes to a limit's current window, where the window is one week.

settingsGroupCount.description: How many optimizers in one visibility group are switched on.

settingsGroupInvisibleNote.message: Only what the page is allowed to ask for changes. If one of these breaks something, it is a bug.
settingsGroupInvisibleNote.description: Note under the "Nothing on the page changes" group heading.

settingsGroupInvisibleTitle.description: Heading for the group of optimizers whose effect is not visible on the page.

settingsGroupNoticeableNote.message: These change what a page looks like or how it behaves. They save the most.
settingsGroupNoticeableNote.description: Note under the "You will see these" group heading.

settingsGroupNoticeableTitle.description: Heading for the group of optimizers whose effect is always visible.

settingsGroupSubtleNote.message: Content can arrive later than it would have, or at a lower resolution than the page asked for.
settingsGroupSubtleNote.description: Note under the "You may notice these" group heading.

settingsGroupSubtleTitle.description: Heading for the group of optimizers whose effect is sometimes visible.

settingsHoldoutLabel.description: Label for the choice of how many page loads are deliberately left unoptimized so savings can be measured by comparison.

settingsHoldoutOff.description: Option in the savings-measurement picker: hold no page loads back at all.

settingsHoldoutOffHint.message: No page loads are held back. Savings are then the estimator's guess at what a refused request weighed, plus arithmetic wherever the original size of a rewritten image is already on file. The dashboard says which part is which.
settingsHoldoutOffHint.description: Hint shown when no page loads are held back. States what the savings figure is then made of — a model, plus arithmetic where an original size is known — because the product's central claim is that measured and modelled figures are kept apart.

settingsHoldoutOnHint.message: $PERCENT$% of page loads are deliberately left unoptimized, so "saved" can be the difference between two sets of real page loads rather than a model of one. A held-back load costs the bytes the optimizer would have removed — real money on a metered connection. A site also gets up to three of them before this rate applies, so there is something to compare against at all.
settingsHoldoutOnHint.description: CONSENT DISCLOSURE, not marketing copy. This is the only place the user is told that measuring the extension's own savings spends their data, and the sentence naming that cost — a held-back load costs the bytes the optimizer would have removed, real money on a metered connection — must stay as blunt as it is here. Do not soften it, do not drop it, do not move it behind the benefit.

settingsHoldoutPercent.description: Option in the savings-measurement picker: the share of page loads deliberately left unoptimized.

settingsImpactAria.description: Accessible name for the three-segment meter beside an optimizer. Not shown on screen; the level word beside it is.

settingsImpactHigh.description: Relative amount of data one optimizer is expected to save. Relative, not a percentage — the actual saving depends on the site.

settingsImpactLow.description: Relative amount of data one optimizer is expected to save. Relative, not a percentage — the actual saving depends on the site.

settingsImpactMedium.description: Relative amount of data one optimizer is expected to save. Relative, not a percentage — the actual saving depends on the site.

settingsLevelBalanced.description: Preset: the invisible changes plus smaller images and no autoplay. What a fresh install ships with.

settingsLevelBalancedHint.message: Everything in Light, plus smaller images and no autoplay. Pages can arrive a little later or a little softer. Recommended.
settingsLevelBalancedHint.description: Hint shown when the Balanced preset is chosen. "softer" means a lower-resolution image than the page asked for.

settingsLevelCustom.description: Shown in place of a chosen level when the switched-on Data Saver features match none of the three presets.

settingsLevelCustomHint.message: Your own selection, made under Advanced. Choosing a level above replaces it.
settingsLevelCustomHint.description: Hint shown when the switched-on features match none of the three presets. It warns that picking a preset overwrites the selection, because nothing else on the page would say so.

settingsLevelLabel.description: Label for the three-way choice between the preset feature sets (Light, Balanced, Maximum). This is the only Data Saver control most people will touch.

settingsLevelLight.description: Preset: only the changes that are invisible on the page.

settingsLevelLightHint.message: Only changes you cannot see: the light version of a page, no analytics beacons, images below the fold left until you reach them.
settingsLevelLightHint.description: Hint shown when the Light preset is chosen. Names what it does, not how many switches it represents.

settingsLevelMaximum.description: Preset: every change, including the two that visibly alter a page.

settingsLevelMaximumHint.message: Everything, including system fonts and video that waits for a click. Pages will look different. This saves the most.
settingsLevelMaximumHint.description: Hint shown when the Maximum preset is chosen. The admission that pages look different is the load-bearing part — do not drop it.

settingsLimitAdd.description: Submit button for the add-limit form.

settingsLimitAllowanceButton.description: The allowance cell in the limits table, which is also the button that opens the editor.

settingsLimitChangeError.description: Fallback error when pausing, resuming, granting bytes to, editing or removing a limit fails.

settingsLimitCreated.description: Confirmation after adding a limit. Names the site key that was actually stored, which is the only signal that a pasted address was trimmed to a domain.

settingsLimitEditAria.description: Accessible name for the allowance button in one row, since the visible label is a size and does not say which site it belongs to.

settingsLimitEditTitle.description: Tooltip on the allowance button in the limits table.

settingsLimitPeriodLabel.description: Label for the choice of window a new limit's allowance covers, read as "Per: Day".

settingsLimitPeriodTitle.description: Tooltip on one option of the window picker, spelling out the abbreviated option label.

settingsLimitReplaced.description: Confirmation after adding a limit for a site that already had one. Saying it was replaced matters: the form used to overwrite silently.

settingsLimitResets.description: When one limit's allowance next restarts, e.g. "Resets in 6 hours" or "Resets on browser close". WHEN is a phrase, not a date, so it can be either.

settingsLimitShapeHardHint.message: Nothing changes on this site until its allowance is spent. After that only pages themselves load.
settingsLimitShapeHardHint.description: Hint shown when "Stop at the limit" is chosen for a site limit.

settingsLimitShapeLabel.description: Label for the choice of what a new site limit does as it fills. Deliberately the same words as the plan's version of this choice: it is the same question about a smaller scope, and two names for it would read as two mechanisms. Replaces a switch labelled "Hard cap", which named the mechanism and left the other option unnamed.

settingsLimitShapeProgressiveHint.message: On this site: video and audio stop at 60% of the allowance, images and web fonts at 85%, everything but the page itself at 100%.
settingsLimitShapeProgressiveHint.description: Hint shown when "Cut back gradually" is chosen for a site limit. The same three thresholds as the plan's version of this hint, at the scope of one site.

settingsLimitSiteLabel.description: Label for the field naming the site a new limit applies to.

settingsLimitSitePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the website field of the add-limit form. A domain name.

settingsLimitSizeLabel.description: Label for the field holding how many bytes a new limit allows.

settingsLimitSizePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the allowance field of the add-limit form. Byte units are the ones the extension prints elsewhere.

settingsLimitSizeUnreadable.message: Could not read "$INPUT$" as a size. Try 500 MB or 1.5 GB.
settingsLimitSizeUnreadable.description: Error when the allowance typed into the add-limit form cannot be parsed. Quotes back exactly what was typed.

settingsLimitsEmpty.message: No site limits yet. Add one below, or set one from the popup while you are on the site.
settingsLimitsEmpty.description: Empty state shown in place of the limits table, naming both ways to add a limit.

settingsLimitsListTitle.description: Heading over the list of existing site limits.

settingsLimitsNoteMany.description: Count of site limits, shown beside the panel heading, when there is more than one.

settingsLimitsNoteNone.description: Value under "Site limits" in the settings rail when no limit is set. Blank was read as an item still loading, next to "No plan set" and "Off" on the two items above it.

settingsLimitsNoteOne.description: Count of site limits, shown beside the panel heading, when there is exactly one.

settingsLimitsReadError.description: Fallback error when the list of limits cannot be loaded.

settingsLimitsSub.message: Cap one heavy site on its own, without touching the rest of your browsing.
settingsLimitsSub.description: One line under the "Site limits" heading, saying how a per-site limit differs from the allowance over everything in Data plan.

settingsLimitsTitle.description: Heading of the section listing per-site allowances.

settingsMeter.description: Text label on the progress bar for one limit.

settingsMonthCalendar.description: Month window option: from the start of the current calendar month.

settingsMonthModeHint.message: A calendar month is not the same window as your plan's cycle. The cycle is the one the projection uses.
settingsMonthModeHint.description: Hint under the month window choice, keeping it distinct from the billing cycle set in the plan panel.

settingsMonthModeLabel.description: Label for the choice of what the month period on the other surfaces covers. The quoted phrase is the label those surfaces use.

settingsMonthRolling.description: Month window option: a rolling thirty days ending today.

settingsNavDashboard.description: Navigation link to the full-tab dashboard page.

settingsNavLabel.description: Accessible name for the two-link navigation bar (Dashboard, Settings). Not shown on screen.

settingsNavSettings.description: Navigation link to this options page. It is the current page.

settingsOptimizeLoading.message: Data Saver settings are still loading.
settingsOptimizeLoading.description: Shown when a site is added to the exception list before the settings have arrived.

settingsOptimizeReadError.description: Fallback error when the Data Saver settings cannot be loaded.

settingsOptimizeSaveError.description: Fallback error when a Data Saver change cannot be written.

settingsOrdinalFirst.description: English ordinal for a day ending in 1 (but not 11), e.g. "21st". Return the number alone in a language with no ordinal suffix.

settingsOrdinalOther.description: English ordinal for every other day, e.g. "17th". Return the number alone in a language with no ordinal suffix.

settingsOrdinalSecond.description: English ordinal for a day ending in 2 (but not 12), e.g. "22nd". Return the number alone in a language with no ordinal suffix.

settingsOrdinalThird.description: English ordinal for a day ending in 3 (but not 13), e.g. "23rd". Return the number alone in a language with no ordinal suffix.

settingsPackHosts.description: The hostnames one image service rule is allowed to touch, listed under its description so the scope is legible.

settingsPacksIntro.message: Image services that serve a smaller version of the same file from the same path. Byte Budget rewrites the request before it is sent, so the smaller file is what crosses the wire. If pictures from one service look wrong, switch that service off rather than excluding the whole site.
settingsPacksIntro.description: Introduction to the per-image-service switches, ending with the remedy for a service that returns a wrong-looking image.

settingsPageTitle.description: Browser tab title for the options page.

settingsPause.description: Button that suspends a limit for one hour. Abbreviated to fit a row of buttons.

settingsPauseTitle.message: Stop refusing anything for an hour. The counter keeps running.
settingsPauseTitle.description: Tooltip on the Pause button. The second sentence matters: pausing does not stop the measurement.

settingsPeriodDay.description: Option in the window picker: the allowance covers one day.

settingsPeriodMonth.description: Option in the window picker: the allowance covers one month.

settingsPeriodSession.description: Option in the window picker: the allowance covers this browsing session and resets when Chrome closes.

settingsPeriodWeek.description: Option in the window picker: the allowance covers one week.

settingsPlanCycleCalendar.description: First option in the reset-day picker: the cycle follows the calendar month rather than a chosen day.

settingsPlanCycleDay.description: One reset-day option, e.g. "The 17th". The ordinal suffix is formed in English by the page; a language that does not use one can render the placeholder alone.

settingsPlanCycleHint.message: Any day up to the 28th, so the date never moves in February.
settingsPlanCycleHint.description: Hint under the reset-day picker, giving the reason the choice stops at 28: a cycle anchored to the 31st would move in February, and the reset date is the value a person checks against a paper bill.

settingsPlanCycleLabel.description: Label for the picker choosing which day of the month the plan's cycle restarts.

settingsPlanCycleLine.message: This cycle started $FROM$ — day $ELAPSED$ of $TOTAL$, resets $WHEN$.
settingsPlanCycleLine.description: Where the current billing cycle has got to.

settingsPlanEchoEmpty.description: Shown under the plan size field while it is empty, so clearing it is understood as a deliberate action rather than a blank.

settingsPlanEchoReads.description: Echoes back the size the field was parsed as, on every keystroke. This exists because "1,5 GB" means 1.5 GB in some locales and 15 GB in some parsers, and a size field must never take a number and mean a different one.

settingsPlanEchoUnreadable.message: Cannot read that as a size.
settingsPlanEchoUnreadable.description: Shown under the plan size field when what has been typed cannot be parsed as a byte figure.

settingsPlanEmpty.message: No plan set. Until there is one the dashboard can only show totals: no share of a plan, no projection, and nothing for a plan alert to check.
settingsPlanEmpty.description: Empty state in the plan panel, listing exactly which figures stay unavailable while no plan is set.

settingsPlanNeedsSize.message: Set a plan size for this to apply to.
settingsPlanNeedsSize.description: Shown when the user chooses what the plan does as it fills, but no plan size has been entered yet.

settingsPlanNoAllowance.message: $CHOICE$ is selected, so there is no allowance over everything. Nothing is refused and plan alerts have nothing to measure against.
settingsPlanNoAllowance.description: Shown when a plan size is set but the user chose to measure only. CHOICE is the name of that option, so the sentence names the control the reader would change.

settingsPlanNote.description: Note in the plan panel header once a plan is set: its size and when the cycle next restarts.

settingsPlanNoteUnset.description: Note in the plan panel header when no plan size has been entered.

settingsPlanRemoved.description: Confirmation after clearing the plan size field and saving.

settingsPlanSaveError.description: Fallback error when saving the plan fails and the failure carries no message of its own.

settingsPlanSavedCalendar.description: Confirmation after saving a plan whose cycle follows the calendar month.

settingsPlanSavedDay.description: Confirmation after saving a plan whose cycle restarts on a chosen day of the month.

settingsPlanScope.message: Byte Budget sees one Chrome profile on this device, so its total is always lower than your carrier's — often by a lot.
settingsPlanScope.description: Footnote under the plan controls. A scope disclosure: the extension cannot see other browsers, profiles or devices, so its figure is not the carrier's figure. Keep that admission — do not soften it.

settingsPlanShapeHard.description: Option: change nothing until the plan is spent, then refuse everything but the page itself. Was "Hard stop".

settingsPlanShapeHardHint.message: Nothing changes until the plan is spent. After that only pages themselves load, until the allowance rolls over, or you pause it, or you add bytes to this window.
settingsPlanShapeHardHint.description: Hint shown when "Stop at the limit" is chosen, naming the three ways out of it.

settingsPlanShapeLabel.description: Label for the choice of what the plan does as it is spent: track only, cut back gradually, or stop. Was "As the plan fills", which described the mechanism rather than the moment a person is thinking about.

settingsPlanShapeProgressive.description: Option: as the plan fills, refuse progressively more kinds of request across every site. Was "Shed weight", which named nothing a person could picture.

settingsPlanShapeProgressiveHint.message: Across every site: video and audio stop at 60% of the plan, images and web fonts at 85%, everything but the page itself at 100%.
settingsPlanShapeProgressiveHint.description: Hint shown when "Cut back gradually" is chosen, listing the three thresholds and what each refuses.

settingsPlanShapeWatch.description: Option: keep counting against the plan but never refuse a request. The honest name for having no allowance at all. Was "Just measure".

settingsPlanShapeWatchHint.message: Nothing is ever blocked, and there is no allowance for an alert to check — so plan alerts stay quiet. The dashboard still measures the cycle against the plan.
settingsPlanShapeWatchHint.description: Hint shown when "Just track it" is chosen. It names the consequence — plan alerts cannot fire — because that setting is on by default.

settingsPlanSizeLabel.description: Label for the text field holding the plan's total allowance, e.g. "15 GB".

settingsPlanSizePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the plan size field, showing the shape of an answer. Byte units are the ones the extension prints elsewhere.

settingsPlanSizeUnreadable.message: Could not read "$INPUT$" as a size. Try 15 GB or 500 MB.
settingsPlanSizeUnreadable.description: Error on saving the plan when the typed size cannot be parsed. Quotes back exactly what was typed.

settingsPlanSub.message: How much data you have, when it resets, and what should happen when it runs out.
settingsPlanSub.description: One line under the "Data plan" heading, naming the three things the section holds. Deliberately short: the detail is on the controls themselves.

settingsPlanTitle.description: Heading of the section where the user enters their carrier's data allowance and the day it resets.

settingsPlusCheckError.message: Could not reach the subscription service.
settingsPlusCheckError.description: Status after a forced subscription check fails. Deliberately does not suggest anything is locked, because nothing is.

settingsPlusChecked.description: Status after a forced subscription check succeeds.

settingsPlusChecking.description: Status while a forced subscription check is in flight.

settingsPlusDetailExpired.message: The settings you had configured are still there and still running. Subscribing again makes them editable.
settingsPlusDetailExpired.description: Detail line after a lapse. States the central promise of the paid tier: a ceiling limits what you can change, never what you already have.

settingsPlusDetailFree.message: Everything that measures, reports and limits your usage is working. Plus adds the settings below.
settingsPlusDetailFree.description: Detail line for a free install that has never subscribed.

settingsPlusDetailMonth.message: Billed monthly. Everything below is unlocked.
settingsPlusDetailMonth.description: Detail line under the state heading for a monthly subscriber.

settingsPlusDetailPastDue.message: The last payment did not go through. Everything is still unlocked while the card is retried — update it to keep it that way.
settingsPlusDetailPastDue.description: Detail line when the subscription is past due.

settingsPlusDetailTrial.message: Everything below is unlocked. The trial ends $WHEN$, and nothing you have set will be deleted when it does.
settingsPlusDetailTrial.description: Detail line during a trial. The second clause is a promise the product keeps: settings made during a trial survive its end, they just stop being editable.

settingsPlusDetailYear.message: Billed yearly. Everything below is unlocked.
settingsPlusDetailYear.description: Detail line under the state heading for a yearly subscriber.

settingsPlusIncludedTitle.description: Heading above the list of paid features.

settingsPlusItemCompare.message: The per-site with-and-without comparison under Data Saver results
settingsPlusItemCompare.description: List item on the Plus section. Refers to the dashboard savings panel.

settingsPlusItemHistory.message: Reporting and export past $DAYS$ days, up to everything on disk
settingsPlusItemHistory.description: List item on the Plus section.

settingsPlusItemHosts.message: Which third-party hosts a site's bytes came from
settingsPlusItemHosts.description: List item on the Plus section. Refers to the dashboard site drill-down.

settingsPlusItemLimits.message: Site limits past $COUNT$, and weekly, monthly or per-session windows
settingsPlusItemLimits.description: List item on the Plus section.

settingsPlusItemSaver.message: Every Data Saver change on its own, the six image services, and the holdout that measures what they saved
settingsPlusItemSaver.description: List item on the Plus section.

settingsPlusItemUnits.message: Units, and whether a week and a month are calendar or rolling
settingsPlusItemUnits.description: List item on the Plus section.

settingsPlusLockAppearanceAdvanced.message: Units, and how weeks and months are counted, are part of Plus. The defaults are 1 kB = 1000 B and rolling windows.
settingsPlusLockAppearanceAdvanced.description: Lock notice inside the Appearance Advanced disclosure. Names the defaults so a free user knows what they are getting rather than what they are missing.

settingsPlusLockHistory.message: The free tier reports the last $DAYS$ days. Everything before that is still recorded and still on this device — Plus is what shows it.
settingsPlusLockHistory.description: Lock notice above the export controls. The second sentence is essential: the ceiling is on what is drawn and exported, never on what is kept, and nothing is deleted.

settingsPlusLockMoreLimits.message: The free tier keeps $COUNT$ site limits. Your plan-wide limit does not count towards that, and the limits you already have keep working.
settingsPlusLockMoreLimits.description: Lock notice above the add-limit form once the free ceiling is reached. The last clause is a promise the product keeps: nothing already configured is disabled or deleted.

settingsPlusLockSaverAdvanced.message: Choosing each change yourself is part of Plus. The three levels above set the same switches, and Balanced is what a fresh install runs.
settingsPlusLockSaverAdvanced.description: Lock notice at the top of the Data Saver Advanced disclosure. Second sentence matters: it tells a free user the level picker is not a lesser version of this, it is the same switches.

settingsPlusManage.description: Opens the account page on extensionpay.com, where a subscription can be changed or cancelled.

settingsPlusOpenError.description: Status when one of the extensionpay.com pages could not be opened in a new tab.

settingsPlusPriceLine.description: The two prices, shown only to someone who is not subscribed. The amounts are substituted so the currency and format come from one place in the code.

settingsPlusPrivacyBlurb.message: A never-connected free install makes no subscription request. Starting a trial, subscribing or restoring creates an opaque account key stored on this device. Byte Budget sends that key to extensionpay.com about four times a day; it never sends usage, site names, limits or settings. The reply can contain an account email and subscription details. Byte Budget keeps only the paid state, dates and plan interval and discards the rest. Card details stay on ExtensionPay and Stripe's pages.
settingsPlusPrivacyBlurb.description: Full disclosure of the subscription check. Load-bearing: it is what replaces the extension's former claim to make no network requests at all. Do not shorten in translation.

settingsPlusPrivacySummary.description: Summary of a collapsed disclosure describing the only network request the extension makes.

settingsPlusTermsBlurb.message: Byte Budget's developer, not Google, sells Plus. Monthly and yearly plans renew until cancelled. Manage subscription opens the account page where you can cancel future renewals; access continues through the paid period. For a billing error or refund request, contact xiangli3625@gmail.com within 14 days of the charge. Requests are reviewed individually, and your legal consumer rights are not limited.
settingsPlusTermsBlurb.description: Terms of sale shown inside the Plus section: seller identity, renewal and cancellation behavior, and the refund contact policy. Keep the distinction from Google explicit.

settingsPlusTermsSummary.description: Summary that opens the Plus terms of sale and refund policy.

settingsPlusRecheck.description: Forces a subscription check rather than waiting for the scheduled one. The only place in the extension that makes a network request on demand.

settingsPlusRestore.description: Opens the login page on extensionpay.com. The route back to a subscription someone already owns, on a second machine or after a reinstall.

settingsPlusStale.message: Last confirmed $WHEN$. Nothing has been locked because of it.
settingsPlusStale.description: Shown when the subscription check has not succeeded recently. The second sentence is the failure policy: a check that cannot be made never removes access.

settingsPlusStartTrial.description: Primary action for someone who has not used their trial. Opens extensionpay.com.

settingsPlusStateExpired.description: State heading after a subscription or trial has ended.

settingsPlusStateFree.description: State heading for an install that has never subscribed. Names the tier, rather than describing the person as lacking something.

settingsPlusStatePaid.description: State heading when a paid subscription is active.

settingsPlusStatePastDue.description: State heading when the subscription is active but the last charge failed. Both halves are true and both are needed: access continues while the card is retried.

settingsPlusStateTrial.description: State heading during a free trial.

settingsPlusSub.message: Everything that measures your usage is free and always will be. Plus adds the settings and the history for people who want to tune it.
settingsPlusSub.description: Sub-heading of the Plus section. States what is NOT behind the paywall first, because measurement and the honesty disclosures never are.

settingsPlusSubscribe.description: Opens the payment page on extensionpay.com.

settingsPlusTitle.description: Heading of the paid-tier settings section. A product name; usually not translated.

settingsPlusUnlock.description: Link on a lock notice. Goes to the Plus section of this same page.

settingsPrivacyBlurb.message: Byte Budget records bytes per site per day and per hour, which hosts a site's bytes came from, and one row per page load holding the site and origin — never a path or a query string. None of that measured data is uploaded. Preferences follow you through Chrome sync; site names, limits and exceptions do not leave this profile. A connected Plus account is checked separately with ExtensionPay, as disclosed in the Plus section. The figures cover this Chrome profile on this device: other profiles, browsers, devices and everything outside Chrome are invisible.
settingsPrivacyBlurb.description: PRIVACY DISCLOSURE. States exactly what is recorded, what leaves the profile, and the scope limit of every figure in the product. It matches the published privacy policy, so nothing here may be generalised, shortened or made more reassuring.

settingsPrivacySummary.description: Label on the disclosure holding the full privacy statement.

settingsRailAlerts.description: Sidebar item for the section holding the two desktop-notification switches.

settingsRailAppearance.description: Sidebar item for the section holding the theme and the toolbar badge.

settingsRailLabel.description: Accessible name for the sidebar listing the six sections of this page. Not shown on screen.

settingsRailLimits.description: Sidebar item for the section holding per-site data allowances.

settingsRailOff.description: Shown under "Data Saver" in the sidebar while the feature is switched off. Its own message rather than the picker option of the same name: this one describes a whole feature's state, and a language may inflect the two differently.

settingsRailPlan.description: Sidebar item for the section holding the plan size, its reset day, and what happens when it runs out.

settingsRailPlus.description: Rail item for the paid-tier section. The product name is Byte Budget Plus; this is the short form used on a narrow rail.

settingsRailPlusOff.description: Rail value under Plus when the install is on the free tier. Names the tier the person is on, not something missing.

settingsRailPlusOn.description: Rail value under Plus when the install has a paid subscription.

settingsRailPlusTrial.description: Rail value under Plus while a free trial is running.

settingsRailPrivacy.description: Sidebar item for the section holding what is recorded, how long it is kept, export and delete.

settingsRailSaver.description: Sidebar item for the section holding the optimizer. "Data Saver" is the product's name for it and is used on every surface.

settingsReadError.description: Fallback error when the preferences cannot be loaded.

settingsRemoveTitle.message: Deletes the limit and lifts anything it is refusing right now
settingsRemoveTitle.description: Tooltip on the Remove button. Says the refusals stop immediately, because Remove is the user's escape hatch from a site that has stopped working.

settingsResetsOnClose.description: Value in the Resets column for a session limit, which has no fixed reset time.

settingsResume.description: Button that starts enforcing a paused limit again.

settingsResumeTitle.message: Start enforcing this limit again now

settingsRetentionDays.description: One retention option, and the way the current retention is named in the delete warning.

settingsRetentionForever.description: Retention option: never delete daily rows on age.

settingsRetentionHint.message: Hourly detail is kept for 3 days whatever this says. Shortening it deletes the days outside the window at the next tidy-up, which runs every six hours.
settingsRetentionHint.description: Hint under the retention picker, naming what the setting does not cover and when a shortened window takes effect.

settingsRetentionLabel.description: Label for how long daily rows are kept before being deleted.

settingsSaveError.description: Fallback error when a preference cannot be written.

settingsSaved.description: Shown after a change is written, in the small status slots beside a panel heading, where nothing else is a sentence.

settingsSavedSentence.description: Shown after a change is written, in the plan panel's status line, where the surrounding messages are sentences.

settingsSaverStateOff.message: Off. Pages load exactly as the site sends them.
settingsSaverStateOff.description: Secondary line beside the master switch while Data Saver is off. It replaces the old "Off until you switch it on" label above the heading: the state belongs on the control, not over the title.

settingsSaverStateOn.message: On for every site except the ones you list below.
settingsSaverStateOn.description: Secondary line beside the master switch while Data Saver is on.

settingsSaverSub.message: Ask sites for less, so a page costs fewer bytes to open.
settingsSaverSub.description: One line under the "Data Saver" heading, saying what the feature does in terms of the outcome rather than the mechanism.

settingsSaverSwitchLabel.description: Label on the master on/off switch. Same words as the section heading, on the control rather than the heading.

settingsSaverTitle.description: Heading of the section holding the page and network optimizers.

settingsSaving.description: Shown while a change is being written. Trailing character is a single ellipsis.

settingsSectionAdvanced.description: Label on the collapsed disclosure at the foot of the Appearance section, holding units and the week and month rules. A separate message from the Data Saver one because the two disclosures hold unrelated things and a language may name them differently.

settingsSiteErrorBadEnding.message: "$HOST$" does not end in something like .com or .org.
settingsSiteErrorBadEnding.description: Error when the last label of what was typed cannot be a top-level domain.

settingsSiteErrorEmpty.description: Error when the website field is empty, or holds something with no hostname in it at all.

settingsSiteErrorIpv6.message: Byte Budget matches sites by name, so an IPv6 address cannot be used.
settingsSiteErrorIpv6.description: Error when an IPv6 literal is typed. Names the reason: rules are matched by domain name, so such a limit would exist and never fire.

settingsSiteErrorNoEnding.message: "$HOST$" has no domain ending. Try "$HOST$.com", or paste the address.
settingsSiteErrorNoEnding.description: Error when a bare name was typed with no dot in it. Suggests the correction rather than silently creating a limit that can never match a request. HOST appears twice on purpose: once as typed, once inside the suggestion.

settingsSiteErrorScheme.message: Only http and https addresses can be used here.
settingsSiteErrorScheme.description: Error when a pasted address uses a scheme the extension cannot meter, e.g. ftp: or file:.

settingsSiteErrorShape.message: "$INPUT$" is not a website address. One looks like example.com.
settingsSiteErrorShape.description: Error when what was typed cannot be a hostname at all. Quotes back exactly what was typed and shows the shape of a valid answer.

settingsStatusNearly.description: Status of a limit at or above 85% of its allowance.

settingsStatusOver.description: Status of a limit whose allowance is fully spent.

settingsStatusPaused.description: Status of a limit that is not currently refusing anything, when the resume time is not known.

settingsStatusPausedUntil.description: Status of a limit that is not currently refusing anything, and when it starts again.

settingsStatusWithin.description: Status of a limit below 85% of its allowance.

settingsStorageBaselinesDesc.message: Original sizes of images a pack can rewrite. Not covered by the retention setting.
settingsStorageBaselinesDesc.description: What one baseline row is. The second sentence is a disclosure: this store ages out on its own schedule, not on the retention chosen above.

settingsStorageBaselinesLabel.description: Storage report row: recorded sizes of image variants an image-service rule can rewrite.

settingsStorageColHolds.description: Column heading in the storage report: what one row of that store is.

settingsStorageColRows.description: Column heading in the storage report: how many rows that store holds.

settingsStorageColStore.description: Column heading in the storage report: the name of one store.

settingsStorageDailyDesc.message: One row per site per day
settingsStorageDailyDesc.description: What one row of the daily store is.

settingsStorageDailyLabel.description: Storage report row: the daily totals store.

settingsStorageError.message: Could not read the storage report.
settingsStorageError.description: Fallback error when the storage report cannot be read.

settingsStorageEstimate.message: The browser estimates $SIZE$ on disk for this extension, rounded for privacy and including the settings.
settingsStorageEstimate.description: The disk figure, with both of its caveats: the browser rounds it deliberately, and it covers more than the stores listed above.

settingsStorageHostsDesc.message: Which hosts a site's bytes came from
settingsStorageHostsDesc.description: What one row of the per-host store is.

settingsStorageHostsLabel.description: Storage report row: the per-host detail store.

settingsStorageHourlyDesc.message: One row per site per hour, kept 3 days
settingsStorageHourlyDesc.description: What one row of the hourly store is, and how long it survives.

settingsStorageHourlyLabel.description: Storage report row: the hourly totals store.

settingsStorageModelDesc.message: The estimator, per host and type
settingsStorageModelDesc.description: What one row of the size estimator is.

settingsStorageModelLabel.description: Storage report row: the learned size estimator.

settingsStorageNoEstimate.message: The browser does not report how much disk this is using.
settingsStorageNoEstimate.description: Shown instead of a disk figure when the browser gives no estimate.

settingsStorageNotReported.description: Shown in the Rows column when the worker did not return a count for that store.

settingsStorageReading.description: Shown while the storage report is being counted. It is read on demand because counting every store is real work.

settingsStorageSummary.message: What this is costing on disk
settingsStorageSummary.description: Label on the collapsed disclosure holding the row counts and disk estimate.

settingsStorageVisitsDesc.message: Site and origin only — no path, no query
settingsStorageVisitsDesc.description: What one page-load row holds. The exclusion is the point: it is what keeps this from being a browsing history.

settingsStorageVisitsLabel.description: Storage report row: the one-row-per-page-load store.

settingsThemeAuto.description: Theme option: follow whatever the operating system is set to.

settingsTierColAt.description: Column heading: the share of the allowance at which this step begins.

settingsTierColRefuses.description: Column heading: what this step of a limit stops loading.

settingsTierColSee.description: Column heading: what the step looks like on the page.

settingsTierExplainer.message: "$SHED$" walks down these steps as the allowance fills. "$STOP$" skips all of them until 100%, and then applies the last one.
settingsTierExplainer.description: Explains how the two limit shapes relate to the table of steps below it.

settingsTierNote.message: The page's own HTML always loads, at every step, so the site can say what happened instead of showing a browser error. Pause a limit for an hour, add bytes to the current window, or remove it, at any time.
settingsTierNote.description: Note under the table of limit steps. The first sentence is the reason the document is never blocked; the second lists the ways out of a limit.

settingsTierSummary.message: What a limit does as it fills
settingsTierSummary.description: Label on the collapsed disclosure holding the table of what each step of a limit refuses.

settingsTrackHostsHint.message: Off makes the per-site drill-down poorer and the database smaller. Rows already recorded stay until they age out.
settingsTrackHostsHint.description: Hint under the per-host switch, naming both what is lost and what switching it off does not do.

settingsTrackHostsLabel.message: Record which hosts a site's bytes came from
settingsTrackHostsLabel.description: Switch for per-host detail inside each site.

settingsUnitsHint.message: A data plan is quoted in decimal units (1 GB = 1000 MB); a file manager counts binary ones (1 GiB = 1024 MiB). The same bytes read as 15 GB or 14 GiB, which is why the unit is always printed.
settingsUnitsHint.description: Hint under the units picker, explaining why the two options exist and why the unit symbol is always shown.

settingsUnitsLabel.description: Label for the decimal/binary byte units picker.

settingsWeekCalendar.description: Week window option: from the start of the current calendar week.

settingsWeekModeLabel.description: Label for the choice of what the week period on the other surfaces covers. The quoted phrase is the label those surfaces use.

settingsWeekRolling.description: Week window option: a rolling seven days ending today.

settingsWeekStartLabel.description: Label for the choice of which weekday a calendar week begins on.
